headline.funnel_interpretation: Egger’s test was not performed because fewer than 10 studies were available. With a small number of studies, the test generally has insufficient power to reliably detect funnel plot asymmetry.
headline.results_interpretation: The pooled analysis of 4 studies yielded an effect size of 0.66 (95% CI: 0.4–1.08), indicating no statistically significant association between zeaxanthin and prostate cancer\aggressive. Although the point estimate suggests a potential inverse relationship, the confidence interval includes the null. These findings were accompanied by substantial heterogeneity (I² = 62.87%), reflecting considerable variability across studies.
